title: Logs and diagnostics
description: Read Flexarr's log, turn up the detail for one area, follow a single playback, collect diagnostics from the apps, and choose whether to send error reports.
text: Flexarr keeps a log of what the server and its apps do. When a film won't play, a scan stalls or Sonarr can't be reached, the log usually says why. It stays on your server: nothing in it is sent anywhere unless you download it and attach it to a bug report yourself. #Reading the log Open Settings › Logs in the web app, as the main profile. The newest entries are at the top. Select an entry to see its details. To narrow it down: Minimum level: show only warnings and errors, say, or everything down to Debug. Area: one part of Flexarr, such as Playback or Library scans, or All areas. Search: any text in the entry. Live: turn it on to watch new entries arrive as they happen. It's handy while you reproduce a problem. Load older at the bottom goes further back. #Following one playback Every time something starts playing it gets a short id, such as 3f9a1c07. The server's lines about that playback show it as #3f9a1c07, and the Apple TV, iPhone and iPad apps attach the same id to what they report. Open an entry and select its playbackId to see only that playback: the whole story, from the server and the device, from start to finish. #Turning up the detail Under Levels, the Default level applies to the whole server. Each area can be set to log more (Debug) or less (Warning) than that. Changes apply straight away, with no restart. Area What it covers General Everything not below, including startup Playback Direct play, transcoding, ffmpeg, downloads to phones Library scans Scanning, reading files, imports Sonarr, Radarr and Seerr Calls to the *arr apps and Seerr Metadata and artwork TVmaze, TMDB, artwork Live TV Dispatcharr channels, the guide, recordings Podcasts Feeds and episode downloads Notifications Push notifications Web requests One line per request. Failures show at Information; set Debug to see every request Apps and browsers What the Apple TV, iPhone, iPad and web app report Tip Chasing a problem? Set its area to Debug, make the problem happen again, then set the area back to Default so the log doesn't fill up. #What the apps send Automatically: warnings and errors from the Apple TV, iPhone and iPad apps, and errors from the web app. They appear under the Apps and browsers area, named after the device. When you ask: Send diagnostics sends a device's recent log in full. On Apple TV, iPhone and iPad it's in the app's Settings › Server › Send diagnostics. Add a note saying what happened and roughly when, then send. Diagnostics go to your server and nowhere else. They're listed under Diagnostics from apps at the bottom of the Logs page, with the device, app version, profile and when they arrived, and a Download button for each. #Download diagnostics Download diagnostics, at the top of the Logs page, makes a zip to attach to a bug report. It holds: the server's logs diagnostics sent from the apps your settings, with every key and password blanked a description of the server: Flexarr version, operating system, ffmpeg, free space and library sizes #What's taken out API keys, passwords, sign-in tokens and playback session ids are removed before anything is written: keys and passwords become ***, and long tokens become a short #id. That's true of the server's log files, what the apps send and the diagnostics zip, so the zip is safe to attach to a public bug report. Titles and file names do appear in the log, because they're what you need to work out what went wrong. Look through the zip first if that matters to you. #How long logs are kept Logs are kept for 14 days, and the log folder is capped at 100 MB, oldest files first. Change both under Retention on the Logs page: Keep for (days) and Largest size (MB). The server starts a new file each day (flexarr-20261027.log, say), and another if one day's passes 10 MB. Each line is a JSON object, so other tools can read them. Install Log folder Mac ~/.flexarr/logs Docker /config/logs (and docker logs flexarr) Anywhere else logs in Flexarr's data folder, or set Flexarr__Logs__Directory #Error

title: Troubleshooting
description: Fixes for the most common Flexarr problems, from an app that can't find your server to playback that won't start, HDR, sound and connecting away from home.
text: Most problems have a short fix. Find yours below. If it isn't here, or the fix doesn't work, the log usually says what's wrong: see Logs and diagnostics, and where to get help at the end. #Connecting #The app can't find my server The iPhone, iPad and Apple TV apps look for Flexarr on your home Wi-Fi. If Looking for Flexarr… never finds it: Check the server is running. On another device on the same network, open http://<server>:8383 in a browser, using the computer's name or IP address. If that doesn't load, the problem is the server, not the app. See your install guide: Mac, Synology, Unraid or Docker. Check you're on the same network. The device must be on the same Wi-Fi as the server, not a guest network and not mobile data. Check local network access (iPhone and iPad). The app asks to find devices on your local network the first time it opens. If you said no, turn it back on in the iPhone's Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › Flexarr. Type the address instead. Choose Enter an address instead and type the address that worked in the browser, such as http://192.168.1.20:8383. You'll still get a code to approve. If the browser test works but discovery doesn't, your router may block devices from announcing themselves to each other. Typing the address always works. #The app says the server hasn't been set up A new Flexarr server has no owner until someone sets it up in a browser. The app shows the steps; here they are in full: On a computer on your home network, open the server's address (the app shows it) in a web browser. Enter the server's setup code (it's in the server's log; First setup says where for your install) and choose Set up Flexarr. That browser becomes the server's owner, with no key needed. Go to Settings › Security › Connect a device and type in the code the app is showing. The app moves on by itself once you have. See First setup. Set up Flexarr only appears to a browser on your home network, using the server's own name or IP address. It won't appear over the internet, or once someone has set the server up. If someone else in the house set it up, ask them to approve your code from their browser. #I can't connect away from home Flexarr isn't on the public internet. Away from home, the apps reach it over Tailscale. Check each of these: Remote access is on. In the web app, Settings › Access › Away from home should say On: Flexarr is available on your tailnet. If it says Tailscale isn't installed or isn't connected, install Tailscale on the server and sign in first. Tailscale is connected on your phone or tablet, signed in to the same tailnet. You have a profile. Under People on your tailnet, each Tailscale account must be linked to a profile. Anyone without one is turned away. The app has picked up the address. It learns the Tailscale address from the server and uses it when the home address can't be reached. If remote access was turned on after the app connected, close and reopen the app at home once. In the app, Settings › Server shows both addresses and which one it's using. Full details are in Away from home. #Your library #New downloads don't appear Flexarr rescans each library every 12 hours, and straight away when Sonarr, Radarr or Lidarr tell it something's arrived. If new downloads take hours to show up, the webhook is missing or failing. In Flexarr, open Settings › Connections and find Webhooks. Copy the address for each app. In Sonarr (and Radarr, and Lidarr), go to Settings › Connect › + › Webhook, paste the address, set the method to POST, and tick On Import, On Upgrade, On Rename and On Delete. Use Test in Sonarr to check it gets through. If Sonarr runs in Docker on the same computer as Flexarr, use host.docker.internal in the address in place of the computer's name. If you made a new webhook secret in Flexarr, the old addresses stop working: copy the new ones in. If the webhook arrives but nothing appears, the paths probably don't match. title: Frequently asked questions
description: Short answers about Flexarr's cost and licence, what you need to run it, privacy, the apps, and how many people can use it.
text: #The basics #What is Flexarr? Flexarr is a media server you run yourself, on a computer at home. It organises your films, TV, music and podcasts and plays them on the web, Apple TV, iPhone and iPad. There's no Flexarr account and no cloud service in the middle: your library and everything about it stays on your server. It's built to sit alongside Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr, which fetch and organise your media, and Seerr, which handles requests. #Is it free? Yes. The server and the iPhone and iPad app are both free, with no subscription and no adverts. Flexarr is licensed under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. You can use it, change it and share it for any noncommercial purpose: at home, for yourself and your family, or in a charity, school or other noncommercial organisation. You can't sell it or use it in a commercial product or service without a separate licence from the author. Because it restricts commercial use, Flexarr is source-available rather than open source in the Open Source Initiative's sense. The source code is all on GitHub. If you'd like to support it, there's a Sponsor button on the GitHub page. #Do I need Sonarr, Radarr or Lidarr? Flexarr works best with them, and they're where most of its information comes from. Here's what each one adds: Sonarr and Radarr supply the posters, artwork and details for your shows and films, with no extra accounts or API keys. Without them, Flexarr still finds and plays your video files, and takes artwork and details from any .nfo files and images beside them (as Kodi, Jellyfin and Plex users often have), from TVmaze for shows, and from TMDB for films with a free key of your own. See Without Sonarr and Radarr. They also power Coming soon, deleting through Sonarr and Radarr, and "find a better copy" in Library health. Lidarr supplies artist pictures, album covers and the split into albums, EPs and singles. Music works without it, using the tags in your files and any artwork in their folders. Seerr lets you request films and shows from Discover. Without it, Discover shows your own library by genre. Cast and crew for TV shows come from TVmaze, which needs no setup. Podcasts are built in and need none of these apps. See Connect Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and Seerr. #What hardware do I need? Any computer that stays on at home and can see your media: A Mac, Apple silicon or Intel. Flexarr runs natively, and uses the Mac's graphics chip to convert video when a device needs it. See Install on a Mac. A NAS or Linux machine with Docker. The image runs on Intel/AMD (x86-64) and ARM (arm64) machines. See Synology, Unraid and Docker. Most of the time the server does very little: the Apple TV, iPhone and iPad play files as they are, and the server sends the bytes. It works harder when it has to convert a video for a device that can't play it, such as a web browser with a 4K HEVC film. A graphics chip that can do this (Apple's VideoToolbox, Intel Quick Sync, VA-API or NVIDIA NVENC) makes a big difference. The apps need iOS, iPadOS or tvOS 18.2 or later. More in What you need. #Using it #Can several people use it? Yes. Each person gets a profile with their own Continue Watching, watched history, playlists, podcasts and settings, which follow them from device to device. Profiles can have a PIN, and can be kept out of particular libraries. A shared Apple TV can ask who's watching each time Flexarr opens. The main profile manages the server; the others can change their own playback and podcast settings. See Profiles. #How many people can watch at once? Flexarr doesn't limit how many screens play at once. In practice the limit is your server and your network. Files played as they are (most playback on Apple TV, iPhone and iPad) take very little work, so many can run at once. Converted streams take real work. Flexarr converts up to 3 videos at once by default, which suits a Mac mini. When that's full, the next person to start one is told the server is busy, and one profile can't take every slot.
